name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: Article 4: 5 consecutive years' residence (absences under 1 year permitted without breaking continuity), full civil rights and good conduct, Arabic literacy, no communicable diseases, and either beneficial expertise or a legitimate income source.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years' residence while meeting the language, health, and self-sufficiency conditions.

requirement_groups.name: Discretionary fast track (Arab nationals / noble services)

requirements.blocker_text: Article 6: nationals of Arab countries, individuals who have rendered 'noble services' to Syria, or those who previously held Arab nationality may bypass the standard Article 4 conditions entirely, at ministerial discretion. No fixed residency period or objective test is specified -- this is a wide, ministerially-controlled discretionary gate.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of Arab nationality, prior Arab nationality, or noble services (discretionary route)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: absences under 1 year do not break the 5-year continuity requirement

sources.title: MENA Rights Group -- hosted English translation of Syria's Nationality Act (Legislative Decree No. 276 of 1969): Articles 4 (standard naturalisation conditions) and 6 (discretionary exceptions)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Syria). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2 NGO-hosted-translation limitation as the other Syria citizenship files; no Ministry of Interior government portal for naturalisation applications was locatable/fetchable in this build. Article 6's discretionary track is genuinely wide -- 'noble services' is undefined in the text reviewed and left to ministerial judgment, a real, sourced example of executive discretion rather than a codified objective standard, distinct from Lebanon's similarly discretionary Article 3 'estimable services' track built earlier in this dataset but framed here without even Lebanon's minimum-service-years alternative. dual_citizenship_allowed set null -- no renunciation or dual-nationality clause was found in Articles 4 or 6 as reviewed; not asserted as permitted or barred. GOVERNANCE-TRANSITION CAVEAT, SAME AS THE DESCENT FILE: this 1969 Act predates the December 2024 change of government; whether and how the transitional administration is currently applying naturalisation decisions under it was not independently confirmed in this build.
